outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a personal tracking dashboard meant to organize publicly available information for research purposes. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.area: Cybersecurity & enterprise tech, led by NetApp, Zscaler and CrowdStrike
strongest.reason: the whole group advanced as broader risk appetite improved on a cooler-than-fully-expected CPI print and retreating oil prices, with agentic-security enthusiasm continuing to support sector sentiment
Bitcoin and Ethereum both rebounded as markets digested mixed CPI/PPI data without a sharp negative reaction, reversing part of the prior pullback tied to Fed-hike fears

weakest.area: Robotics, across nearly every name in the group
weakest.reason: Tesla, Intuitive Surgical, Teradyne and UBTECH all fell together; Intuitive's slide reflects the ongoing JNJ Ottava competitive overhang, while the others cooled off from recent rallies without a clear shared catalyst

weakest.area: AI software, led by Adobe's post-earnings slide
weakest.reason: Adobe fell despite strong AI-revenue growth as investors focused on softer recurring-revenue trends and a pending CEO transition, while Palantir also gave back some of its PwC-alliance-driven gains

outlook.nextStep: Next week's Sept 15-16 FOMC decision is now the dominant catalyst, with rate-hike odds near 87% after Friday's hotter-than-expected core CPI reading — worth tracking closely given the direct line to yields, the dollar, and risk appetite broadly. The Strait of Hormuz conflict remains the bigger wildcard despite Friday's pullback in oil, since strikes continued on both sides; the sharp, uneven moves across individual robotics and chip names (Teradyne, Arm, UBTECH) look more like noise from a single session than a new trend worth acting on yet.

signals.title: US-Iran tanker conflict grinds on even as oil retreats
signals.body: US and Iranian forces continued tit-for-tat strikes near the Strait of Hormuz over the past 24-48 hours, with Iran's IRGC navy targeting tankers and vessels tied to the US, and US forces disabling or destroying several Iranian oil carriers in response. Despite the ongoing escalation, Brent and WTI both pulled back roughly 3% from their recent highs.
signals.focus: the conflict remains the single biggest swing factor for oil and risk appetite; today's pullback in crude is worth watching for follow-through rather than treating as resolution

signals.title: Fed rate-hike odds jump to roughly 87% after hotter core CPI
signals.body: August CPI came in close to headline expectations, but the core reading (ex food and energy) was a touch hotter than forecast, pushing markets' odds of a rate hike at next week's Sept 15-16 FOMC meeting to around 87%, up sharply from roughly 60-74% earlier in the week. Treasury yields still eased on the day as oil's retreat offset some inflation concern.
signals.focus: the most important economic event of the month, worth tracking closely; day-to-day repricing of hike odds is probably better watched than traded on

signals.title: Oracle beats on cloud growth, but gives back early gains as capex/debt scrutiny grows
signals.body: Oracle's fiscal Q1 2027 results topped estimates, with cloud infrastructure revenue up roughly 30% year-over-year on surging AI demand; shares initially jumped as much as 4% after hours before fading during the regular session as investors weighed the company's rising debt load (reportedly near $125 billion) tied to its AI buildout. Elsewhere in the AI-infrastructure trade, Dell and HPE both surged on continued enthusiasm for AI hardware spending.
signals.focus: a genuine growth story worth a closer look, though the capex/debt debate is probably better watched over the next few quarters than reacted to on one session's fade

signals.title: Adobe slides on cautious outlook despite strong AI-revenue growth and CEO transition
signals.body: Adobe's Q3 FY2026 results showed AI revenue accelerating and confirmed a CEO succession plan, but shares fell as investors focused on slowing recurring-revenue growth and a more cautious Q4 outlook. Peers Intuit and ServiceNow were little changed, suggesting the reaction is specific to Adobe rather than a broader software rotation.
signals.focus: a company-specific guidance concern worth a closer look rather than a signal to extend to the broader software group

signals.title: EDA names diverge further as Cadence stabilizes and Synopsys extends its rebound
signals.body: Cadence traded roughly flat, stabilizing after last week's sharp selloff tied to Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 autonomous chip-design demo, while Synopsys extended its recovery, helped by analyst commentary (Mizuho) arguing the episode reinforces rather than undermines the long-term case for agentic-AI-assisted EDA tools.
signals.focus: worth a closer look over the next few weeks to see which read on the Kimi K3 story the market ultimately favors

signals.title: Robotics names broadly pull back as JNJ's Ottava overhang persists for Intuitive Surgical
signals.body: Tesla, Intuitive Surgical, Teradyne, and UBTECH all fell together. Intuitive's decline extends a valuation reset tied to JNJ's FDA-authorized Ottava soft-tissue robotic surgery platform, a direct challenge to Intuitive's roughly 80% market share; Tesla cooled off even as it touts its new Cybercab robotaxi launch and a reported 1 million miles of unsupervised autonomous driving.
signals.focus: the JNJ/Intuitive competitive story looks structural and worth a closer look, while the broader group's one-day pullback is probably better watched for follow-through than acted on

signals.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum rebound as markets shrug off mixed inflation data
signals.body: Both Bitcoin and Ethereum bounced back, with Ethereum outperforming, as traders digested a mixed CPI/PPI picture without a sharp risk-off reaction, reversing some of the recent pullback tied to Fed rate-hike fears.
signals.focus: a tentative stabilization signal worth tracking over the next few sessions rather than reacting to on a single bounce
